Since it was stripped of planetary status, Pluto’s defenders have been fighting the decision – and they’re only getting more passionate

Twenty years ago, Pluto got demoted. After a vote by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in August 2006, Pluto was relegated from major planet to dwarf planet status. Our solar system dropped from nine planets to eight. At the time, many scientists were unhappy with the decision. Two decades on, the debate is, if anything, even more polarised.

e8542fcdd3aa.title: Starwatch: Sagitta’s arrow shape makes it easy to see against a dark sky
e8542fcdd3aa.summary:
The third-smallest constellation can be found partway along one of the imaginary lines of the summer triangle

We are on the hunt for another small, northern summer constellation this week: Sagitta, the arrow. Although it consists of just a handful of faint stars, Sagitta’s distinctive shape (it really does look like an arrow) makes it easy to identify against a dark sky.

The chart shows the view looking up towards the zenith while facing south from London at 22.30 BST on Monday.</

f076746c05ef.title: Too much coffee may weaken bones, study finds
f076746c05ef.summary: Following nearly 10,000 older women for 10 years, researchers found that tea drinking was associated with slightly higher hip bone density. The findings suggest tea may offer a small bone-health boost, while excessive coffee could carry some drawbacks.

6f9a585188de.summary: NASA-funded studies suggest Earth’s climate has been influenced by both the Sun’s travels through dense regions of the Milky Way and the violent superflares of its youth. Those events may help explain ancient ice ages as well as how early Earth stayed warm enough for liquid water when the Sun was much dimmer.

aa707d3da1f8.title: “Broken heart syndrome” can look just like a heart attack. This test can tell them apart
aa707d3da1f8.summary: “Broken heart syndrome” can mimic a heart attack so closely that patients often need invasive testing to tell the difference. Researchers have now developed the BioTAK score, which combines biological sex with blood biomarkers to identify the condition before cardiac catheterization. In a validation study of nearly 1,800 patients, it correctly classified almost 90% of participants.

c9f5540d2b9d.title: Scientists discover why snake embryos twist into spirals
c9f5540d2b9d.summary: Snake embryos begin life curled into a distinctive right-handed spiral, and scientists may finally know why. Their bodies grow faster than their guts, creating a tether that forces the lengthening embryo to buckle and twist inside the egg. Researchers reached the conclusion after studying more than 900 embryos and using CT scans to reveal the hidden anatomy behind the coils.
